And so is killing someone's favorite board.
The migration process is simple. Connect your source platform, pick your documents, choose your destination. Editable shapes appear on the other side.
Add the Chrome extension. It detects your active session automatically. No OAuth dance, no developer portal, no API tokens. Just log into your diagramming tool. That's sufficient. We're not picky.

Browse your complete document library from the extension panel. Every document. Even the ones you forgot about in 2019. Search, filter, select individually or in bulk. We won't judge how many you have. Actually, we might.

Choose your destination: FigJam, Miro, or a structured ZIP archive. The conversion engine parses bounding boxes, coordinate systems, color spaces, text markup, and connector routing, then reassembles it all as editable shapes on your target platform. 146 shape types mapped. Every connector preserved. Your boards arrive editable, not as screenshots you'll have to recreate.

Process your document library in batches. We recommend starting with a few test documents to verify results, then scaling up. Minutes per batch, not the months you were quoted by that consulting firm. You know the one.

Bounding boxes, x/y positions, width, height, rotation: extracted at source fidelity. Your shapes will be exactly where you left them. Which is more than can be said for your original platform's export tools.

Download portable JSON with complete document structure: pages, blocks, lines, properties, text markup, container hierarchies. Your data, in a format that doesn't require a proprietary viewer to open.

Lucid (Chart + Spark) to FigJam. Miro to FigJam. Lucid to Miro. FigJam to Miro. 146 shape types mapped across platforms (flowcharts, BPMN, ERDs, whiteboards, sticky notes, freehand pen strokes, cloud architectures). Connectors, styles, and text recreated via native APIs. It's almost like your boards teleported.

No API keys. No OAuth applications. No developer portals. No "please contact your account administrator." The extension uses your existing browser session. If you can see your documents, we can extract them.
Extraction runs in your browser. Document data is parsed locally before transmission.* Your org's network diagrams don't take a detour through someone else's servers.
*Platform migrations require server-side processing for API coordination. We had to draw the line somewhere. Pun intended.
